source.title: Sparse Autoencoders Encode Both Concepts and Functions: The Downstream Geometry of Feature Effects
source.authors: Phu Gia Hoang; Anwoy Chatterjee; Tanmoy Chakraborty; I. Gurevych; Subhabrata Dutta

record.tranche_reason: The study measures the geometry of downstream logit effects caused by SAE feature ablations. It does not test superposition or the representational geometry, completeness, or canonicality named in the claim versions; its findings concern a related but different object.
record.gate_note: The paper reports downstream effects of SAE-feature ablation, not whether sparse features are represented as overlapping directions. Its feature-selection counts and task-accuracy ablations concern identifying task-associated features and their causal contribution, not superposition, so they are not catalog rows. The geometry findings are recorded as related findings that fit none of the listed versions.
record.test_reason: The study uses SAE features from Gemma-2-2B as its objects. It measures the geometry of the logit changes caused by ablating each feature across contexts. It does not test superposition, polysemanticity, whether a dictionary recovers sparse features, whether SAE features are complete, stable or canonical units, or the dimensionality of represented features. The authors say the local decoder perturbation is a fixed direction, and that their object is downstream effect space, not representation. The findings therefore fit no version.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that stable one-dimensional downstream effect directions are rare. Value-like features show low-dimensional structure more often than pointer-like ones, though usually across several directions. Mapped pointer-like effects are predominantly diffuse. A feature can be interpretable and causally relevant without giving a stable steering direction.
record.recipe_differences: The study does not implement or reproduce the original toy-model superposition method; it measures downstream logit effects of SAE-feature ablations in Gemma-2-2B.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors limit their conclusions to Gemma-2-2B, post-layer-12 SAEs of width approximately 65k, selected feature populations, sampled contexts, and target-position logit readouts. Outcomes also differ across SAE variants and feature/task populations.

fits_no_version.finding: Pointer-like SAE features (ICL tasks): of 80 mapped cases, 74 have unresolved or diffuse downstream logit-effect geometry; 3 are directed rays and 3 are global low-dimensional subspaces.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE features that contribute causally to prompt-local operations rarely produce a context-invariant logit-effect direction.

fits_no_version.finding: RAVEL value-like features more often show structured low-dimensional logit effects (14.0% ReLU, 36.3% TopK, 30.3% Matryoshka of eligible features). Directed rays are rare (5, 14 and 6 features).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Ablation effects of factual-attribute SAE features usually span several output directions rather than one steering vector, with rates depending on SAE architecture.

record.problems: All experiments use one base model, Gemma-2-2B. The authors state that conclusions are conditional on selected features and at most 64 active contexts per feature; many features lack sufficient evidence or receive no defined geometry label. Measurements use target-position logit readouts, and the authors note that geometry may differ at the SAE site or in other settings.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-version result rows were omitted. Feature-selection counts and task-accuracy ablation results (Sections 4.1–4.5, Tables 1–2) were left out because they measure feature association or task contribution, not superposition or any listed version.

untested.parts: All: no toy models, no sparsity sweep, no overlap or geometry of stored features.
All: no capacity manipulation or link between feature importance and dedicated dimensions.
All: whether features spread across neurons or are recoverable by SAEs is not tested; the SAEs are taken as given.

Completeness, stability across training runs, and canonicality of SAE features in the representation. The study's 'stability' concerns downstream logit-effect direction across contexts, a different construct.
Dimensionality of the represented or superposed features. The study measures downstream effect-cloud dimensionality, not representational dimensionality.

record.verdict_notes: Row numbers check out against Tables 4–5: 239−159=80 mapped; 1078/7715=14.0%; 424/1167=36.3%; 530/1750=30.3%. Rows r2–r4 omit the axis counts (12, 13, 11) and directional-mixture counts (0, 11, 1) from Table 5; these are minor completeness gaps. Changed relation from 'discusses/T6' to 'uses_without_test/T4' because SAE dictionary features are the study's working tool, but no version is tested either way. The authors caution that diffuse logit effects may coexist with low-dimensional local perturbations at the SAE site.

versions.untested_parts: Toy-model superposition, overlap, near-orthogonality, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry.
Whether limited capacity causes polysemanticity or allocates dedicated dimensions to important features.
Whether polysemantic neurons arise for reasons other than capacity pressure.
Whether LLM features spread across neurons or are recovered as sparse features by a dictionary.
Whether SAE features are complete, stable, canonical units of model representation.
The dimensionality of the represented or superposed features; the study measures downstream logit-effect geometry instead.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-2B
rows.operation_detail: Measured FEGA geometry labels for downstream logit effects of ablating pointer-like SAE features.

conditions.value: ReLU, TopK, and Matryoshka Batch TopK
239 selected features across the reported tasks and SAE variants; mapped cases only for the mapped-geometry summary

rows.value: Of 239 selected features, 159 had undefined geometry. Of the 80 mapped cases, 74 were unresolved high-dimensional or diffuse; 3 were directed rays and 3 occupied global low-dimensional subspaces.
rows.note: Aggregate across pointer-like candidates as reported by the authors; the study states that stable low-dimensional structures are rare among mapped cases.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-2B
rows.operation_detail: Measured FEGA geometry-label distribution for downstream logit effects of ablating RAVEL-selected features.
rows.value: 5,185 insufficient effect evidence; 4,760 undefined; 1,860 unresolved high-dimensional or diffuse; 1,078 combined G-kD, residual-low-dimensional, 1D-diffuse, and G-2D (14.0% of eligible features); 5 directed rays.
rows.note: These are downstream logit-effect geometries, not the representational geometry of the SAE features.
